evidence.label: OpenSpec homepage
evidence.summary: Official site describes repo-resident specs, proposals, designs, tasks, spec deltas, and broad agent support.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: OpenSpec is the clearest front-door competitor for gzkit: it makes change intent reviewable before implementation. gzkit should borrow spec-delta ergonomics while preserving ADR, OBPI, ledger, and receipt rigor.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Seeded as primary comparator; extension catalog makes trajectory worth monthly tracking.

evidence.label: GitHub Spec Kit repository
evidence.summary: Repository includes specify-plan-tasks workflows, brownfield examples, and community extensions.

evidence.label: Spec Kit site
evidence.summary: Official site frames Spec Kit as GitHub-maintained SDD tooling.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Spec Kit has stronger adoption UX and public extension gravity. gzkit should answer with a better operator entry point and structured workflow data, not weaker governance.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Seeded as primary UX comparator for requirements-design-tasks flow.

evidence.label: Kiro homepage
evidence.summary: Official page emphasizes requirements, system design, and tasks before implementation.

evidence.label: Kiro feature specs docs
evidence.summary: Feature-spec documentation describes product-driven requirements and implementation tasks.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Kiro's strength is not deeper truth; it is less friction at the moment of intent capture. gzkit can close that gap with operator-first workspace flow and bugfix-spec routing.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Seeded as context-package and spec-registry comparator.

evidence.label: Tessl SDD registry tile
evidence.summary: Registry tile packages a spec-driven development methodology.

evidence.label: Tessl SDD launch post
evidence.summary: Launch post explains framework and registry positioning.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Tessl is a clean signal that reusable context packages matter. gzkit's version must add manifest, provenance, injection scanning, and receipt evidence.

evidence.label: Specmatic CDD docs
evidence.summary: Docs frame API specs as executable contracts with compatibility checks and service virtualization.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Specmatic is narrower than gzkit but more mature where it operates. gzkit should make every external contract surface mechanically witnessed, including CLI, schemas, ledger, skills, and docs examples.

evidence.label: BMAD Method repository
evidence.summary: Repository presents scale-adaptive planning tracks, specialized agents, and workflow modules.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: BMAD's advantage is guided adoption and workflow menus. gzkit should improve skill routing and onboarding, but not confuse persona ceremony with receipt-backed state.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Promoted from missed comparator to primary watch.

evidence.label: GSD repository
evidence.summary: Repository advertises multi-runtime installs, planning/verification agents, context warnings, and worktree execution controls.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: GSD is stronger on runtime portability and fast workflow controls. gzkit should copy multi-runtime parity pressure and security posture while rejecting un-witnessed auto-chaining.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Promoted from missed comparator to primary watch.

evidence.label: Superpowers repository
evidence.summary: Repository describes an agentic skills framework and software development methodology.

evidence.label: Subagent-driven development skill
evidence.summary: Skill specifies fresh subagent per task and two-stage spec/code review.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Superpowers has a crisp review architecture. gzkit should encode that as typed review receipts and pipeline dispatch attestation, not as narrative review claims.

evidence.label: ce-compound skill listing
evidence.summary: Listing points to EveryInc's compound-engineering skill package.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Compound Engineering's core lesson is that review outcomes should become future working memory. gzkit should make that human-reviewed and ledger-witnessed.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Added as skill-design and grill-dialogue reference.

evidence.label: grill-me skill
evidence.summary: Skill packages a forcing-function review dialogue.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: The relevant borrowing is the questioning tactic, not the artifact shape. gzkit's grill answers should update JSON and then generated reports.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Added as reference standard after operator explicitly required following agentskills.io.

evidence.label: Agent Skills home
evidence.summary: Home page describes skills as folders of instructions, scripts, and resources.

evidence.label: Agent Skills specification
evidence.summary: Specification defines SKILL.md plus optional scripts, references, and assets directories.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Agent Skills is the packaging reference for this radar skill. Its concrete lesson is portable execution assets and progressive disclosure, not repo-global automation.

evidence.label: Better Spec homepage
evidence.summary: Homepage advertises initialization from GitHub Spec Kit.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Better Spec is a front-door signal. gzkit should improve entry friction but explicitly reject prompt-only source-of-truth.

evidence.label: Specledger homepage
evidence.summary: Homepage emphasizes spec deltas, checkpoints, session indexing, and multi-repo coordination.

evidence.label: Specledger Go package
evidence.summary: Package docs describe CLI commands for specs, issues, dependencies, and context.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: Specledger overlaps with gzkit's ledger instinct but productizes recall and dashboards. gzkit should keep the ledger local and auditable while improving searchable report and memory surfaces.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Seeded as durable spec-governance reference, not direct SDD product.

evidence.label: OpenAPI specification
evidence.summary: Official site hosts the versioned OpenAPI Specification.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: OpenAPI shows durable specs win by becoming multi-implementation truth. gzkit should use this as a maturity reference for its CLI/schema/ledger/skill contract surfaces.

competitor_snapshots.status_delta: Seeded as durable cross-vendor specification reference.

evidence.label: OpenTelemetry specifications
evidence.summary: Official docs list specification, protocol, agent-management protocol, and semantic-convention versions.

competitor_snapshots.agent_analysis: OpenTelemetry is a reference for governed vocabulary, compatibility, and cross-implementation semantics. gzkit's analog is not telemetry; it is governance proof semantics.

operator_decisions.decision: B+ - seeded registry plus active discovery because we do not know what we do not know.
B- - report with suggested moves, then design discussion to modify recommendations before governance mutation.
C - report includes both product snapshots and strength-pattern mapping.
Markdown is governed by JSON for key fields; Python may accompany the skill to enforce projection.
Scripts stay portable with the skill; deterministic execution assets belong under the skill package.
The competitor radar report lives under artifacts/reports.
The operator authors nothing; the report is agent-authored from evidence JSON and grill answers.

suggested_moves.title: Make external-strength absorption a recurring foundation doctrine candidate
suggested_moves.recommendation: Keep as pool for now; monthly reports should cite it as the doctrine home for borrowed workflow pressure.
suggested_moves.mechanical_witness: Monthly report checksum plus evidence URLs; future promotion adds schema/validator/ledger witness for comparator intake.
suggested_moves.rationale: This move protects gzkit's identity: borrow mechanisms only when they become ledger/receipt/validator/attestation surfaces.

grill_questions.question: Are we copying a product or absorbing a mechanism?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: Absorbing mechanisms only: front-door clarity, compounding feedback, and contract proof.

grill_questions.question: Which gzkit invariant must not weaken?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: Ledger-of-truth beats agent-trust; reports cannot mutate governance without design approval.

suggested_moves.title: Build an operator-first spec workspace without lightening governance
suggested_moves.recommendation: Promote later as feature work only after the radar grill confirms exact workflow and witness requirements.
suggested_moves.mechanical_witness: Workspace JSON with proposal/design/tasks/spec-delta fields and ADR/OBPI routing receipts.
suggested_moves.rationale: Competitors are better at the first 10 minutes. gzkit should make entry smoother while preserving heavier downstream gates.

grill_questions.question: What is the smallest front-door improvement that still leaves a receipt trail?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: A generated change workspace with spec delta, unchanged behavior, evidence, destination route, and suggested OBPI split.

grill_questions.question: What would make this unsafe?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: Treating the workspace as source-of-truth instead of an intake artifact routed to ADR/OBPI/ledger surfaces.

suggested_moves.title: Add bugfix-spec routing for observed/expected/unchanged behavior
suggested_moves.recommendation: Keep as feature-pool candidate; require explicit unchanged-behavior witness and GHI linkage.
suggested_moves.mechanical_witness: Bugfix spec JSON or Markdown frontmatter with observed, expected, unchanged, tests, route facts, and linked GHI.
suggested_moves.rationale: Bugfix UX is a competitor strength because it captures intent cheaply. gzkit can make that safer with routing thresholds and witnesses.

grill_questions.question: Should bugfix specs ever bypass ADR/OBPI ceremony?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: Only when defect-fix routing thresholds mechanically allow direct fix; otherwise route to OBPI.

grill_questions.question: What field blocks behavior laundering?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: UNCHANGED behavior, backed by tests or explicit waivers.

suggested_moves.title: Turn two-stage review into typed gzkit receipts
suggested_moves.recommendation: Treat as foundation-or-feature candidate during design; the taxonomy affects proof semantics, while CLI/reporting is feature work.
suggested_moves.mechanical_witness: Receipt types for spec-compliance, code-quality, security, performance, overbuild, and integration decision.
suggested_moves.rationale: Superpowers' two-stage review is strong, but gzkit's stronger version is not 'review happened'; it is typed, queryable review evidence.

grill_questions.question: Is this foundation or feature?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: Split: foundation for review-proof semantics, feature for emit/list/validate commands.

grill_questions.question: Which review types must exist first?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: Spec compliance, code quality, security sensitivity, overbuild, and integration decision.

suggested_moves.title: Create governed context-package registry semantics
suggested_moves.recommendation: Keep as feature-pool candidate tied to skill-control-surface contract and content-injection scanning.
suggested_moves.mechanical_witness: Context package manifest with source URL, version/ref, checksum, scan status, allowed consumers, and sync receipts.
suggested_moves.rationale: Competitors are packaging reusable context. gzkit should do the same only when provenance, scan, and consumer controls are first-class.

grill_questions.question: What cannot be trusted from a context package by default?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: Instructions, examples, hidden scripts, and transitive references; all require provenance and scan evidence.

grill_questions.question: What is the first safe package shape?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: Skill-compatible package with manifest, references, scripts, checksum, and allowed-tool declaration.

suggested_moves.title: Make monthly competitor radar a generated report artifact
suggested_moves.recommendation: Land this skill and report artifact now; schedule monthly scans after validation.
suggested_moves.mechanical_witness: Portable skill scripts validate registry, scan JSON, and generated Markdown byte-for-byte.
suggested_moves.rationale: The report itself is the first improvement loop: a governed input to future design discussions, not a one-off chat artifact.

grill_questions.question: Who authors the report?
grill_questions.recommended_answer: The agent authors it from evidence and grill answers; the operator only answers forcing-function questions.
grill_questions.answer: The agent authors it from evidence and grill answers; the operator does not edit JSON or Markdown.
